title: Stimulation of the beta-2-adrenergic receptor with salbutamol activates human brown adipose tissue
authors: Straat ME, Hoekx CA, van Velden FHP, Pereira Arias-Bouda LM, Dumont L, Blondin DP, et al.
population: Ten young lean healthy men; randomised double-blind crossover of a single intravenous bolus of salbutamol 250 µg after oral placebo or propranolol 80 mg, with dynamic [18F]FDG PET-CT
funder: Supported by a Fonds de Recherche du Québec - Santé doctoral award, the GSK Chair in Diabetes of Université de Sherbrooke (to one author), an FRQS salary award, the Dutch Diabetes Foundation, an NWO-VENI grant, a Maria Zambrano fellowship (NextGenerationEU) and the Netherlands Cardiovascular Research Initiative with the Dutch Heart Foundation.
authorConflicts: The authors declare no competing interests associated with this manuscript.
result: Salbutamol increased glucose uptake by brown adipose tissue compared with salbutamol plus propranolol, without changing glucose uptake by skeletal muscle or white adipose tissue; salbutamol-induced uptake correlated with the rise in energy expenditure. Salbutamol raised heart rate acutely by 16.9 beats/min (SD 10.5) and tended to raise energy expenditure by 7.2% (122 kcal/day, p = 0.06), whereas with propranolol energy expenditure fell 9.4%. The authors cite human biopsies and brown adipocytes in which ADRB2, not ADRB3, is the dominant adrenergic receptor.
